steps.subject: [AArch64][Fix] LdSt optimization generate premature stack-popping

evidence: AArch64-related, but it is a load/store optimizer fix around stack pointer folding rather than MC symbol or XRay/table emission.
No clear connection to MCSymbolRefExpr, patchable-function-entry metadata, or AsmPrinter symbol lifetime issues.
features: AArch64 load/store optimizer, stack pointer folding, memory access ordering, prologue/epilogue codegen
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This change tightens AArch64 load/store post-index optimization around stack pointer updates. In AArch64LoadStoreOptimizer::findMatchingUpdateInsnForward it adds a dependency on MCAsmInfo and introduces guards that block SP-folding when Windows CFI/unwind-table handling would be disturbed, and more generally prevent reusing SP as a post-increment base across intervening memory accesses. The accompanying MIR/IR tests codify that premature SP pop/push folding must not occur and adjust expected AArch64 codegen for the affected patterns.
Mechanisms: AArch64 load/store optimizer forward matching now treats SP specially when selecting an update instruction; Optimization is disabled for SP on Windows targets when the function needs an unwind table entry, to avoid unwind/debug info corruption; SP post-increment folding is further blocked if instructions between the memory access and the update may load or store; AArch64 codegen expectations changed from post-indexed stack pop/push forms to explicit separate stack decrement/increment sequences
Touched symbols: AArch64LoadStoreOpt::findMatchingUpdateInsnForward; MCAsmInfo::usesWindowsCFI; needsUnwindTableEntry; mayLoadOrStore; llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/aarch64-ldst-no-premature-sp-pop.mir; llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/arm64-nvcast.ll; llvm/test/CodeGen/AArch64/arm64-windows-calls.ll
Risk relevance: Touches AArch64 assembly emission-adjacent optimization logic that rewrites stack-pointer updates, a common source of miscompiles; Introduces control-flow based gating on unwind-table/Windows CFI state, which can interact with prologue/epilogue and metadata lowering; The new SP-special-case memory-access barrier suggests prior folding could move stack adjustment across memory operations and corrupt stack-relative addressing; Changes codegen shape for stack push/pop patterns, which can affect downstream MC emission and target-specific assumptions
Build risk: Adds an MC header include to a Target/AArch64 codegen source, slightly increasing coupling to MC layer interfaces; Updates MIR and IR tests with stricter instruction-order expectations, indicating output-sensitive behavior; Modifies Windows-specific AArch64 call test expectations, so target-triple-dependent test brittleness is possible

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The change expands ELF section uniquing in MC so that the link-order/linked-to symbol name becomes part of the section identity, not just section name, group name, and unique ID. Summary: The patch changes AArch64 and ARM target transform info so ordered floating-point vector reductions are expanded only when the reduction is actually unordered/relaxed enough to be legal to lower locally. Mechanisms: TargetTransformInfo legality hook for vector-reduction expansion; Fast-math-flag gating of ordered FP reduction expansion via allowReassoc(); NaN-constraint gating for fmax/fmin reductions via noNaNs(); Fallback to legalization for unsupported reductions rather than eager expansion; Codegen tests covering strict and NaN-sensitive vector reduction lowering on AArch64 and ARM

Summary: This AArch64 change extends a peephole/isel optimization so shift-amount masking and compare-to-zero lowering can recognize and reuse AArch64 flag-setting ANDS/TST forms in addition to plain AND. steps.subject: [AArch64] Change AArch64 Windows EH UnwindHelp object to be a fixed object

evidence: Touches AArch64 frame lowering, but the bug signal is about llc crashing in XRay/MCSymbolRefExpr emission, not EH stack layout.
Mechanism is Windows unwind-help fixed-object handling, which is far from emitXRayTable / assembly printer symbol assertions.
features: AArch64 frame lowering, Windows EH unwind help, fixed stack object layout, prologue/epilogue stack accounting
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This change reworks AArch64 Windows EH stack layout so the UnwindHelp slot is modeled as a fixed object in the function’s fixed stack area rather than as a regular stack object, and centralizes fixed-object sizing for Win64 prologues/epilogues, frame-index offset computation, and frame-finalization. The frame lowering logic now accounts for varargs area plus an EH UnwindHelp slot in a shared helper, updates FP/SP-based frame index references to respect that layout, and adds regression coverage for Windows exception-handling and unwind-help addressing patterns.
Mechanisms: AArch64 Win64 stack frame layout calculation; Fixed stack object allocation for EH metadata; Prologue/epilogue frame size and object-offset computation; Frame-index reference selection between SP and FP paths; Windows EH / funclet unwind-help lowering; Alignment-sensitive stack slot placement for varargs and EH data
Touched symbols: AArch64FrameLowering::emitPrologue; AArch64FrameLowering::emitEpilogue; AArch64FrameLowering::getFrameIndexReferencePreferSP; AArch64FrameLowering::processFunctionBeforeFrameFinalized; getFixedObjectSize; getFPOffset; CreateFixedObject; seh-finally.ll

Build risk: Backend codegen change in a target-specific lowering file with multiple regression tests updated; Adds new test coverage for Windows AArch64 exception handling, implying previously fragile or changing behavior; Adjusts stack offsets in ways that can affect generated assembly and unwind info, making test baselines sensitive; Introduces a new fixed-object helper and altered frame-index reference flow, increasing risk of miscompile in corner cases
